newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midco gasoline stable despite Explorer delay.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midco gasoline stable despite Explorer delay.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent unleaded gasoline differentials were steady on Wednesday and remained unaffected by shipping delays on the Explorer pipeline system, traders said.
"I don't think it's that big of a deal. I think it weakened up the Gulf Coast more than it tightened (the Midco)," one trader active in the Chicago and Group Three markets said.
Traders said gasoline shipments on the Explorer pipeline from Houston to Tulsa and on to Chicago were delayed for five days by excess diesel shipments.

The market also yawned at American Petroleum Institute's report late Tuesday of a 1.6 million barrel draw in gasoline stocks that left inventories in the PADD 2 region at 51.3 million barrels for the week ended April 18.
Chicago unleaded gasoline was bid 0.25 cent a gallon under NYMEX May unleaded, and Group Three was bid 0.50 cent under the print, traders said.
Chicago low sulphur diesel was talked 6.0/6.25 cents over NYMEX May heating oil, and Group Three was talked 2.50/2.75 cents over the print.
High sulphur was bid 1.50 cents over the print in Chicago and 5.75 cents over the print in Group Three, where agricultural demand was propping up basis.
